verdict.rationale: OpenClaw calls itself an "Open-Source AI Assistant" and has a public GitHub repository. The docs list an install "from source" option, and community users report inspecting its roughly 700k-line codebase, so the source is readable. However, the evidence never names the license or quotes its terms, so the "open license" part of the story rests only on a marketing label. missing for 10: named license (e.g. MIT/Apache) and its terms, first-party docs on source access and contribution, independent confirmation of license openness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
